views.name: gsod_daily_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS stn,
  wban AS wban,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo, 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(da, 2, '0'))) AS obs_date,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN temp IS NULL OR temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE temp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS temp_f,
  count_temp AS count_temp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN dewp IS NULL OR dewp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE dewp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS dewp_f,
  count_dewp AS count_dewp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN slp IS NULL OR slp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE slp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS slp_mbar,
  count_slp AS count_slp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN stp IS NULL OR stp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE stp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS stp_mbar,
  count_stp AS count_stp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN visib IS NULL OR visib = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE visib END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS visib_miles,
  count_visib AS count_visib,
  -- wdsp and count_wdsp are strings in the DDL; attempt safe cast to float/int
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS wdsp_knots,
  SAFE_CAST(count_wdsp AS INT64) AS count_wdsp,
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(mxpsd AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS mxpsd_knots,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN gust IS NULL OR gust = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE gust END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS gust_knots,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN max IS NULL OR max = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE max END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS max_f,
  flag_max AS flag_max,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN min IS NULL OR min = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE min END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS min_f,
  flag_min AS flag_min,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN prcp IS NULL OR prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL ELSE prcp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS prcp_inches,
  flag_prcp AS flag_prcp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN sndp IS NULL OR sndp = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE sndp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS sndp_inches,
  -- weather occurrence indicators kept as-is (string '1'/'0' or NULL)
  fog AS fog,
  rain_drizzle AS rain_drizzle,
  snow_ice_pellets AS snow_ice_pellets,
  hail AS hail,
  thunder AS thunder,
  tornado_funnel_cloud AS tornado_funnel_cloud,
  -- source shard year for filtering across wildcard tables
  year AS obs_year,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
grain: stn, wban, obs_date  -- one row per station per calendar day (cleaned)

semantic_filters.table_suffix: use WHEN querying a year range via _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'YYYY' AND 'YYYY' or other shard filter; do not select a single shard unless intended

views.description: Normalize and clean GSOD daily observations across year shards: assemble a DATE, convert sentinel missing values to NULL, cast wind fields stored as STRING, and preserve station identifiers for joins. Use this when you need cleaned daily weather measures or to join GSOD to stations or other datasets. | Use for: Daily temperature, precipitation, wind or visibility time series for a station or region; Join cleaned GSOD daily measures to stations for mapping or aggregation; Compute monthly/yearly aggregates while ignoring sentinel missing values; Filter days with precipitation or specific weather occurrences (fog, thunder, etc.)

views.name: stations_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf AS usaf,
  wban AS wban,
  name AS station_name,
  country AS country,
  state AS state,
  call AS call_sign,
  SAFE_CAST(lat AS FLOAT64) AS lat,
  SAFE_CAST(lon AS FLOAT64) AS lon,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(elev, '') AS FLOAT64) AS elev,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', begin) AS begin_date,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `end`) AS end_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
grain: usaf, wban  -- one row per station identifier

semantic_filters.none: Do not filter here; keep full stations dimension. Downstream queries may restrict by country/state or active date ranges.

params.description: Normalized stations dimension: one row per station identifier (usaf, wban) with canonical station name, location, elevation and active date range.
params.when_to_use: Lookup station metadata (name, country, state, call sign) for a given usaf/wban identifier. | Enrich weather/observation rows with station lat/lon/elevation and operational date range for joins by station id. | Filter or aggregate observations by station attributes (country, state) or by station active period. | Compose into larger queries that need a stable, one-row-per-station reference for joining to time-series event/observation tables.
params.output_schema: usaf: Station USAF identifier (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.usaf). | wban: Station WBAN identifier (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.wban). | station_name: Human-readable station name (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.name). | country: Country code for the station (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.country). | state: State code for the station (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.state). | call_sign: Station call sign (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.call). | lat: Latitude as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lat). | lon: Longitude as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lon). | elev: Elevation as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of NULLIF(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.elev, '') ). | begin_date: Station begin date as DATE (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.begin)). | end_date: Station end date as DATE (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.end)).
params.metric: lat = SAFE_CAST(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lat AS FLOAT64) | lon = SAFE_CAST(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lon AS FLOAT64) | elev = SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.elev, '') AS FLOAT64) | begin_date = PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.begin) | end_date = PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.end)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: Join to time-series or observation tables keyed by (usaf, wban) — for example gsod_daily_cleaned (normalized daily observations) — on stations_dim.usaf = gsod_daily_cleaned.usaf AND stations_dim.wban = gsod_daily_cleaned.wban. This is safe because stations_dim is one-row-per-(usaf,wban) (dimension) so joining will not duplicate station-level attributes; the observation table can have many rows per station but that multiplicity is expected. | cardinality-SAFE: Join to sibling normalized event views that reference a single station id per event (for example events_point_reports_normalized) on (usaf, wban) — safe for enrichment because stations_dim provides one row per id. | not-safe-to-join-directly-withOUT-aggregation: Do NOT join stations_dim to any one-to-many aggregated view or table that itself has multiple rows per (usaf,wban) (for example a per-station-per-day aggregated table) if you intend to preserve station-level deduplicated measures; such joins will multiplicatively increase row counts. Instead either (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per (usaf,wban) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate explicitly, e.g., GROUP BY stations_dim.usaf, stations_dim.wban after the join. | examples of unsafe targets: any AGG/RANK/WIN/SET/RESHAPE sibling that produces multiple rows per station identifier (for example tornado_paths_enriched_by_date, storm_peak_intensity_rank, icoads_ship_observation_sequences_win) — these should be joined only after understanding their grain or by aggregating them to station-level. | key guidance: treat (usaf,wban) as the natural composite key. If joining on only one identifier (usaf OR wban) ensure the other identifier is handled consistently (nulls or missing) because stations_dim's uniqueness is defined over the pair. If you need to join by geographic proximity instead of id, do not use this view as an aggregation source; use lat/lon for spatial joins and then re-aggregate as needed.

views.description: Clean stations dimension with standardized column names and parsed numeric lat/lon/elevation and parsed begin/end dates. Use for joins to GSOD or for spatial lookups. | Use for: Lookup station metadata for display or mapping; Join stations to GSOD cleaned daily observations by stn/usaf and wban; Filter stations by country/state or active date ranges

views.name: events_point_reports_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_source,
  timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  DATE(timestamp) AS event_date,
  time AS event_hour_string,
  -- canonical numeric measure: wind.speed, hail.size (hundredths of inch), tornado.f_scale (left as original string)
  CASE WHEN event_source = 'wind_reports' THEN CAST(speed AS INT64)
       WHEN event_source = 'hail_reports' THEN CAST(size AS INT64)
       WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN NULL
       ELSE NULL END AS severity_measure,
  -- original severity text where applicable
  CASE WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN f_scale
       ELSE NULL END AS severity_text,
  location,
  county,
  state,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  comments,
  report_point
FROM (
  -- wind reports across shards
  SELECT 'wind_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, speed, NULL AS size, NULL AS f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.wind_reports*`
  UNION ALL
  -- hail reports across shards
  SELECT 'hail_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, NULL AS speed, size, NULL AS f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.hail_reports*`
  UNION ALL
  -- tornado reports across shards
  SELECT 'tornado_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, NULL AS speed, NULL AS size, f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.tornado_reports*`
)
grain: event_source, event_timestamp, latitude, longitude  -- one row per original report event

params.description: Normalized, one-row-per-original severe-weather report (wind, hail, tornado) with a canonical numeric severity_measure and original severity_text, plus location, time, and free-text comments.
params.when_to_use: Produce a cleaned, unified feed of individual original severe-storm reports (wind, hail, tornado) for filtering, mapping, or time-series counting at the report level. | Aggregate counts or simple statistics (e.g., average wind speed, max hail size) by date, hour, county, state, or spatial buckets by composing GROUP BY on this view. | Join to a spatial or administrative lookup (county/state geometry, station metadata) when each original report should remain one row and not be multiplied by the lookup. | Compose into downstream views that compute event-level metrics (counts, sums, min/max) because the view exposes canonical numeric measure(s) and raw text severity per report.
params.output_schema: event_source: string — source dataset identifier for the original report; derives from the literal labels assigned in each UNION branch ('wind_reports', 'hail_reports', 'tornado_reports'). | event_timestamp: timestamp — original report timestamp column (aliased from timestamp in the source shards). | event_date: date — DATE(event_timestamp), derived from the source timestamp column. | event_hour_string: string — time-of-day string (aliased from time in the source shards); preserves original time formatting from the source. | severity_measure: int64|null — canonical numeric severity measure: for wind_reports this is CAST(speed AS INT64); for hail_reports this is CAST(size AS INT64) (hail size is stored in hundredths of an inch per the view comment); for tornado_reports this is NULL (no numeric canonicalized value). | severity_text: string|null — original textual severity where applicable: for tornado_reports this is f_scale (original F-scale text). | location: string|null — original location text from the source (aliased from location). | county: string|null — original county text from the source (aliased from county). | state: string|null — original state text from the source (aliased from state). | latitude: numeric|null — report latitude from the source (aliased from latitude). | longitude: numeric|null — report longitude from the source (aliased from longitude). | comments: string|null — free-text comments from the source (aliased from comments). | report_point: GEOGRAPHY|string|null — original report_point geometry or representation from the source (aliased from report_point).
params.metric: severity_measure = CASE WHEN event_source = 'wind_reports' THEN CAST(speed AS INT64) WHEN event_source = 'hail_reports' THEN CAST(size AS INT64) WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN NULL ELSE NULL END | severity_text = CASE WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN f_scale ELSE NULL END | event_date = DATE(event_timestamp)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional or one-row-per-geography tables (e.g., a state/county geometry table keyed by (state, county)) ON state = state AND county = county — safe because this view is one-row-per-original-report and county/state lookup is one-row-per-county, so measures from this view are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a stations or single-row-per-station view (e.g., stations_dim keyed by station_id) only if you first ensure a one-to-one match key on this view (this view does not expose station_id by default). | do NOT directly join this view to true one-to-many tables or views (for example: a many-row per report attachments table, or a path/segment table such as tornado_paths_enriched_by_date which represents multi-segment geometries per event) without aggregation — joining a one-to-many child will multiply report rows and thus duplicate counts/sums derived from severity_measure. If you need to combine with a one-to-many child, either: | - aggregate the child to one row per report (e.g., per report identifier or per event_timestamp+location) before joining, or | - aggregate this view after the join (GROUP BY the original report key) to re-summarize measures. | When composing aggregates: treat this view as the atomic report-level grain (event_source, event_timestamp, latitude, longitude). Any join that preserves that grain (one-to-one or many-to-one into this view) will not duplicate measures; any join that expands rows per that grain must be followed by a re-aggregation to avoid measure inflation.

views.description: Normalize and unify point-based event reports (wind, hail, tornado reports shards) into a common schema with consistent timestamp/date, event_type, severity measure and location columns. Useful as a canonical input for aggregations, spatial joins, or time-series analyses across report types. | Use for: time series counts or rates of reports by day/state/event type; top-k highest wind speeds or largest hail sizes over a period; spatial joins to forecast regions or mapping/report clustering; filtering by event_type and computing summary statistics

views.name: tornado_paths_enriched_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  storm_date,
  state_name,
  state_abbreviation,
  state_fips_code,
  COUNT(1) AS paths_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) AS total_length_miles,
  AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) AS avg_length_miles,
  SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) AS total_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) AS total_fatalities,
  SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) AS total_width_feet,
  -- preserve an ordering rank per date for selecting top N by length downstream
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) DESC) AS rank_by_length_per_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.tornado_paths`
GROUP BY storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code
grain: storm_date
state_name
state_abbreviation
state_fips_code

params.description: Daily, state-level aggregates of tornado path counts, lengths, injuries, fatalities, and widths, with a per-date ranking by total path length.
params.when_to_use: Get counts and summary measures of tornado paths for a specific date and state (e.g., How many tornado paths and total length occurred in Iowa on 2015-05-25?). | Compare states on a given storm_date by total tornado path length or rank (e.g., list top N states by total tornado path length for a date). | Time-series analysis at daily granularity per state when using storm_date as the time key (e.g., trends of total_length_miles or total_injured by state over time). | As an aggregated building-block when composing higher-level reports that need one row per (storm_date, state) (e.g., join to a state population dimension to compute per-capita impact). | Filter for top-ranked states per date (using rank_by_length_per_date) before joining to other datasets for detail-level enrichment (but avoid joining to detail tables without re-aggregation).
params.output_schema: storm_date: calendar date of the storm event grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.storm_date | state_name: full state name for the path grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_name | state_abbreviation: postal state code (e.g., 'IA') for the grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_abbreviation | state_fips_code: state FIPS code string/number used for the grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_fips_code | paths_count: COUNT(1) — number of tornado path records aggregated into this (storm_date, state) row; derived from COUNT(1) over tornado_paths rows | total_length_miles: SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) — sum of the length column (in miles) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.length | avg_length_miles: AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) — average of non-zero length values (NULLs and zeros handled) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.length | total_injured: SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) — total injured persons summed from tornado_paths.injured_count across the group | total_fatalities: SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) — total fatalities summed from tornado_paths.fatality_count across the group | total_width_feet: SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) — sum of the width (in feet) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.width | rank_by_length_per_date: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length,0.0)) DESC) — per-storm_date rank ordering states by total_length_miles (ties get same rank); computed from the grouped SUM(length)
params.metric: paths_count = COUNT(1) over rows grouped by (storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code) | total_length_miles = SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) over grouped rows | avg_length_miles = AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) over grouped rows (note: zeros excluded via NULLIF; NULLs are ignored by AVG) | total_injured = SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) over grouped rows | total_fatalities = SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) over grouped rows | total_width_feet = SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) over grouped rows | rank_by_length_per_date = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length,0.0)) DESC) — computed from total_length_miles per state within each storm_date
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a state dimension (e.g., a states_dim view keyed by state_abbreviation or state_fips_code) on state_abbreviation or state_fips_code — safe because this view is one row per (storm_date, state) and the state dimension is one row per state, so measures (paths_count, totals) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a calendar/date dimension on storm_date — safe because calendar dimensions are one row per date and will not multiply aggregated measures. | do NOT join directly to the base tornado_paths table (or any other tornado-path-level/detail table) without re-aggregating the detail side first — joining a one-row-per-(storm_date,state) aggregated view to multiple detail rows will multiply the aggregated measures (double-counting totals). If you need path-level detail together with these aggregates, either: (a) join the detail table aggregated to the same grouping before joining (re-aggregate by storm_date + state), or (b) join detail rows and recompute aggregates from detail after the join. | do NOT join to any one-to-many table (e.g., multiple event reports, station observations, or other detail-level events) using only storm_date or state as the key unless that other side is pre-aggregated to the same grain. Example unsafe joins: joining to events_point_reports_normalized on storm_date will duplicate this view's measures when multiple reports exist for the same date/state. | safe composition for ranking queries: to get top N states by total_length_miles per date, filter on rank_by_length_per_date (e.g., WHERE rank_by_length_per_date <= N) and then join to other one-row-per-state/date resources (like state metadata). Avoid joining to multi-row detail tables after applying the rank filter unless re-aggregation is performed. | when joining to other AGG views that are also one-row-per-(storm_date, state) and use the same grouping keys, the join is safe (measures align row-for-row). Always verify the other view's declared grain matches (storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code). | if you need to combine measures from this view with measures from a different grain (for example, county-level or path-level), bring both sides to a common aggregation grain explicitly (e.g., aggregate path-level data up to storm_date+state before joining) to preserve correct totals.

views.description: Aggregate tornado_paths to produce per-day and per-state summaries (counts, total length, total injuries/fatalities) and include a running rank of paths by length within each date. Useful for daily/state-level reporting of tornado impact and for selecting top-N paths by length per day. | Use for: daily/state tornado burden (counts, injuries, fatalities, lengths); identify top-N longest tornado paths per day (use rank_by_length_per_date <= K); compare average/total path lengths across states or dates

views.name: hurricane_track_points_core

grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation (storm id + timestamp)
views.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of the raw hurricanes table keeping canonical storm identifiers, primary timestamp, canonical lat/lon, common intensity measures from major agencies, and provenance flags. Use this as the base relation for most analyses (filtering, aggregation, windowing, joins). | Use for: Filter track points by basin/season/time range; Compare measures across agencies at same observation time; Aggregate max/min/mean wind or pressure per storm or season; Map storm tracks using canonical lat/lon

views.name: storm_peak_intensity_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  number,
  name,
  iso_time,
  -- preserve canonical coords and primary measures
  latitude,
  longitude,
  wmo_wind,
  usa_wind,
  usa_pressure,
  tokyo_wind,
  cma_wind,
  -- rank of observation within storm by descending usa_wind then descending wmo_wind then earliest time
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) AS rank_by_usa_wind,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) AS rownum_by_usa_wind
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation augmented with per-storm rank

params.description: Per-storm observation rows augmented with an intra-storm rank by peak intensity using USA wind (then WMO wind, then earliest time) — one row per hurricane track observation with position, agency measures, and rank within that storm.
params.when_to_use: Find the strongest observation(s) for each storm according to the 'usa_wind' measure (e.g., peak wind observation per storm). | Compose queries to select top-N observations per storm (e.g., top 1 observation per sid) based on usa_wind with deterministic tie-breaking. | Join storm observation-level attributes (location, time, multiple agency measures) with a per-storm rank to filter or aggregate only peak observations. | Produce storm-level summaries by selecting rows with rank_by_usa_wind = 1 (or other rank thresholds) and then aggregating across storms (seasonal counts, max winds, etc.).
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.sid | season: storm season/year — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.season | number: storm number within season — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.number | name: storm name — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.name | iso_time: observation timestamp (ISO) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.iso_time | latitude: canonical observation latitude — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.latitude | longitude: canonical observation longitude — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.longitude | wmo_wind: WMO-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.wmo_wind | usa_wind: USA/NHC-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_wind | usa_pressure: USA/NHC-reported pressure at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_pressure | tokyo_wind: Tokyo agency-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.tokyo_wind | cma_wind: CMA (China) reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.cma_wind | rank_by_usa_wind: RANK() over partition by sid ordered by usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC — 1 = highest usa_wind (ties produce same rank) | rownum_by_usa_wind: ROW_NUMBER() over same ordering — unique sequence number per observation within the storm (no ties)
params.metric: rank_by_usa_wind = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) | rownum_by_usa_wind = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC)

views.name: storm_observation_deltas_win
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  number,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  usa_latitude,
  usa_longitude,
  usa_wind,
  LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS prev_iso_time,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), SECOND) AS seconds_since_prev,
  -- geographic displacement using canonical lat/lon in degrees (consumer may convert to km/nautical miles externally)
  latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_lat_deg,
  longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_lon_deg,
  -- delta in reporting agency wind
  usa_wind - LAG(usa_wind) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_usa_wind,
  -- simple speed proxy: degrees per second (not true geodesic) exposed for downstream conversion
  SAFE_DIVIDE( SQRT( POW(latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), 2) + POW(longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), 2) ),
    NULLIF(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), SECOND), 0)
  ) AS deg_per_second
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation with differences to previous observation for same storm

params.description: Per-storm-observation deltas: one row per hurricane track observation with time and spatial differences (and wind change) relative to the previous observation for the same storm (sid).
params.when_to_use: Compute per-observation change rates (speed proxy in degrees/sec) for individual storm tracks | Measure displacement or heading approximations between consecutive track points for a storm | Detect rapid intensification or weakening by comparing consecutive usa_wind values | Compose into time-series analyses of storm motion or intensity by joining to storm-level metadata | Filter or flag observations that represent large jumps in position, time gaps, or sudden wind changes
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier from base table `hurricanes.sid`. Primary partition key used to compute deltas. | season: storm season from base table `hurricanes.season` (year). | number: storm number from base table `hurricanes.number` (seasonal index or identifier). | iso_time: observation timestamp from base table `hurricanes.iso_time` (current row). | latitude: canonical observation latitude from base table `hurricanes.latitude` (current row). | longitude: canonical observation longitude from base table `hurricanes.longitude` (current row). | usa_latitude: reporting-agency (USA) latitude from base table `hurricanes.usa_latitude` (current row), if present. | usa_longitude: reporting-agency (USA) longitude from base table `hurricanes.usa_longitude` (current row), if present. | usa_wind: reporting-agency (USA) wind speed from base table `hurricanes.usa_wind` (current row). | prev_iso_time: iso_time of the previous observation for the same sid (computed with LAG over PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time). | seconds_since_prev: TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, prev_iso_time, SECOND) — seconds elapsed since the previous observation for the same sid. | delta_lat_deg: latitude - prev_latitude (difference in degrees latitude vs previous observation). | delta_lon_deg: longitude - prev_longitude (difference in degrees longitude vs previous observation). | delta_usa_wind: usa_wind - prev_usa_wind (change in reported wind vs previous observation). | deg_per_second: sqrt(delta_lat_deg^2 + delta_lon_deg^2) / seconds_since_prev computed with SAFE_DIVIDE and NULLIF to avoid divide-by-zero; units = degrees of lat/lon per second (not geodesic).
params.metric: prev_iso_time = LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | seconds_since_prev = TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, prev_iso_time, SECOND) | delta_lat_deg = latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | delta_lon_deg = longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | delta_usa_wind = usa_wind - LAG(usa_wind) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | deg_per_second = SAFE_DIVIDE( SQRT( POW(delta_lat_deg, 2) + POW(delta_lon_deg, 2) ), NULLIF(seconds_since_prev, 0) )
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to storm-level or one-row-per-sid views/dimensions (e.g., a hypothetical storm metadata view keyed by sid or by (season, number)) on sid — safe because storm_observation_deltas_win is one row per observation (sid+iso_time) and the join target is one-row-per-sid, so each observation remains one row and measures are not duplicated. | You may join to a one-row-per-(sid,iso_time) upstream view/table on (sid, iso_time) — safe because keys align exactly, preserving row cardinality. | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table or view keyed only by sid or (season,number) that contains multiple rows per sid (for example: a table of multiple station reports, multiple observations buckets, or any aggregation partition that produces multiple rows per sid) without first aggregating that table to one row per sid or per (sid,iso_time) as appropriate — such joins will multiply rows and duplicate/overcount the deltas and deg_per_second measures. | Do NOT join to sibling WIN/SET/AGG/RANK views that are many-per-sid (e.g., a per-storm ranked list or per-box aggregates) unless you aggregate their rows to the same grain (sid+iso_time or sid) before joining; if you need to attach many child rows, perform an explicit aggregation (e.g., AVG, MAX) of the child measures to one value per sid or per (sid,iso_time) to avoid measure duplication. | When composing time-series aggregations from this view (e.g., average deg_per_second per storm or per day), aggregate deg_per_second or seconds_since_prev after joining any additional dimensions — do not rely on row counts to normalize rates unless the join keys are cardinality-safe as described above. | If you need geographic distance in meters/nautical miles, compute geodesic distance externally from delta_lat_deg and delta_lon_deg (this view exposes raw degree differences intentionally); converting to true speed requires converting degree-based displacement to distance using an appropriate projection or haversine formula before dividing by seconds_since_prev.

views.description: Compute lead/lag differences in time, position and wind within each storm to support translation speed, displacement, and intensification rate calculations. views.name: icoads_obs_by_callsign_sequences_win
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  callsign,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  hour,
  -- construct an approximate timestamp (UTC-ish) from date parts and fractional hour
  TIMESTAMP_ADD(
    TIMESTAMP(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING), 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING), 2, '0'))),
    INTERVAL CAST(FLOOR(hour) AS INT64) HOUR
  ) + CAST(ROUND((hour - FLOOR(hour)) * 3600) AS INT64) * INTERVAL 1 SECOND AS obs_timestamp,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) AS wind_speed_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) AS sea_surface_temp_c,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) AS sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  -- previous observation timestamp for same callsign
  LAG(
    TIMESTAMP_ADD(
      TIMESTAMP(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING), 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING), 2, '0'))),
      INTERVAL CAST(FLOOR(hour) AS INT64) HOUR
    ) + CAST(ROUND((hour - FLOOR(hour)) * 3600) AS INT64) * INTERVAL 1 SECOND
  ) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS prev_obs_timestamp,
  -- seconds between observations for same callsign (compute diff between obs_timestamp and prev_obs_timestamp produced above)
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(
    TIMESTAMP_ADD(
      TIMESTAMP(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING), 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING), 2, '0'))),
      INTERVAL CAST(FLOOR(hour) AS INT64) HOUR
    ) + CAST(ROUND((hour - FLOOR(hour)) * 3600) AS INT64) * INTERVAL 1 SECOND,
    LAG(
      TIMESTAMP_ADD(
        TIMESTAMP(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING), 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING), 2, '0'))),
        INTERVAL CAST(FLOOR(hour) AS INT64) HOUR
      ) + CAST(ROUND((hour - FLOOR(hour)) * 3600) AS INT64) * INTERVAL 1 SECOND
    ) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour),
    SECOND
  ) AS seconds_since_prev,
  -- spatial deltas
  latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_lat_deg,
  longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_lon_deg,
  -- variable deltas (apply SAFE_DIVIDE consistently and avoid nesting analytic functions)
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) - LAG(SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0)) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_wind_speed_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) - LAG(SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0)) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_sea_surface_temp_c,

If you need attributes from a one-to-many table, first aggregate that table to one row per callsign+obs_timestamp (or per callsign) before joining. | do NOT join to views that contain additional per-observation sequences or windows (e.g., ship_observation_sequences_win or storm_observation_deltas_win) without aligning the partition/order keys — such joins risk creating many-to-many matches across sequence rows and duplicating measures. Instead, join on exact keys (callsign + obs_timestamp) or pre-aggregate to one row per callsign+obs_timestamp. | when composing aggregates: if you aggregate this view (for example, COUNT(*) or AVG(delta_wind_speed_m_s) per callsign or per day), perform aggregation after any join to avoid accidental multiplication; prefer subquery or CTE where this view is first deduplicated to its natural grain (one row per observation) before joining to multi-row tables.

views.name: icoads_top_observations_rank_by_box
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ten_degree_box_number,
  one_degree_box_number,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  callsign,
  deck,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed,10.0) AS wind_speed_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp,10.0) AS sea_surface_temp_c,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure,10.0) AS sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed,10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_wind_speed_desc,
  RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp,10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_sst_desc,
  RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure,10.0) ASC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_slp_asc
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2001_2004`
grain: one row per original observation with ranks assigned within year + box partitions

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; downstream queries typically filter WHERE rank_by_* <= K

params.description: For each original ICOADS observation (one row per observation) this view returns location/time, selected meteorological measures converted to human units, and intra-year+box ranks of each observation by wind speed (descending), sea surface temperature (descending) and sea level pressure (ascending).
params.when_to_use: Find the top (or bottom) observations by wind speed, SST, or sea level pressure within the same year and geographical 10°/1° box partition. | Filter to high-ranked observations (e.g., rank = 1 or rank <= N) within year+box for downstream event/summary analysis. | Join observation-level attributes (callsign, deck, lat/lon, month) to other tables while preserving one-row-per-original-observation semantics. | Build aggregates of top-N observations per box/year by first selecting rows from this view (e.g., WHERE rank_by_wind_speed_desc <= N) and then re-aggregating.
params.output_schema: year: Observation year (directly from base column `year` in the source table). | month: Observation month (directly from base column `month` in the source table). | ten_degree_box_number: 10-degree box identifier containing the observation (directly from base column `ten_degree_box_number`). | one_degree_box_number: 1-degree box identifier containing the observation (directly from base column `one_degree_box_number`). | latitude: Observation latitude in decimal degrees (directly from base column `latitude`). | longitude: Observation longitude in decimal degrees (directly from base column `longitude`). | callsign: Ship/observer callsign identifier for the observation (directly from base column `callsign`). | deck: Deck/platform identifier or code associated with the observation (directly from base column `deck`). | wind_speed_m_s: Wind speed converted to meters per second = SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) where `wind_speed` is the integer/packed value in source table `wind_speed`. | sea_surface_temp_c: Sea surface temperature in degrees Celsius = SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) where `sea_surface_temp` is the integer/packed value in source table `sea_surface_temp`. | sea_level_pressure_hpa: Sea level pressure in hectopascals = SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) where `sea_level_pressure` is the integer/packed value in source table `sea_level_pressure`. | rank_by_wind_speed_desc: Rank() of the observation within the partition (year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number) ordering by wind_speed_m_s descending (NULLs last). Equal values receive the same rank and gaps can occur (standard RANK()). | rank_by_sst_desc: Rank() of the observation within the partition (year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number) ordering by sea_surface_temp_c descending (NULLs last). | rank_by_slp_asc: Rank() of the observation within the partition (year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number) ordering by sea_level_pressure_hpa ascending (NULLs last).
params.metric: wind_speed_m_s = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2001_2004.wind_speed, 10.0) | sea_surface_temp_c = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2001_2004.sea_surface_temp, 10.0) | sea_level_pressure_hpa = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2001_2004.sea_level_pressure, 10.0) | rank_by_wind_speed_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY wind_speed_m_s DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_sst_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY sea_surface_temp_c DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_slp_asc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number ORDER BY sea_level_pressure_hpa ASC NULLS LAST)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables that are one-row-per-key (or can be aggregated to one row) on keys {year, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number} or on observation-level identifiers (e.g., callsign + year + month) — safe because this view is one-row-per-original-observation. Examples of safe joins: |  - Join to a stations_dim (or other single-row station metadata) on callsign (or station id) — safe because stations_dim should be one row per station; joining adds attributes without duplicating observations' measures. |  - Join to a view keyed one-to-one with the original observation (for example icoads_core_sel_basic_obs if it preserves one-row-per-original-observation and shares the same primary key) — safe because keys align 1:1. | Do NOT naively join this view to one-to-many tables or views (for example: multiple event reports per observation, sequences or windows that produce many rows per observation like *_WIN, or any detailed measurement unpivot that expands rows) without re-aggregation, because such joins will multiply rows and therefore duplicate/overcount measures derived from single observations. Specific NOT-SAFE examples: |  - Do NOT join directly to any *_WIN (windowed) views (e.g., icoads_obs_by_callsign_sequences_win, icoads_ship_observation_sequences_win) without aggregating the windowed side to one row per observation first — those views produce multiple rows per observation/time and will multiply counts/sums based on this view's rows. |  - Do NOT join directly to reshape/unpivot outputs (e.g., icoads_measures_unpivot_reshape, agency_measure_unpivot_reshape) which expand measures into multiple rows per observation, unless you first re-aggregate (e.g., count/distinct or MAX) so the join is 1:1. |  - Do NOT join to aggregate views keyed at a coarser grain (e.g., icoads_monthly_agg_per_box, icoads_monthly_agg_per_box_dynamic, seasonal_storm_summary_agg) expecting the aggregate to remain correct unless you aggregate this view to the same grain first — joining a coarser aggregate to these observation rows will duplicate the aggregate when performing sums/counts. | Recommended composition patterns: |  - Filter-then-aggregate: to compute metrics like number of top-N observations per box-year, first SELECT from this view WHERE rank_by_wind_speed_desc <= N and then GROUP BY the desired keys to aggregate; this prevents double-counting and preserves intended semantics. |  - Join for enrichment only on true 1:1 keys: if a dimension/view is guaranteed to be one-row-per-callsign (or per observation id), it can be joined directly. Otherwise, reduce the many-side to one row per join-key before joining (e.g., use MAX/ANY_VALUE or GROUP BY). |  - When composing further rank/window measures, keep the same granular partitioning (year + box identifiers) or explicitly reduce this view to the target partition/grain before computing new window functions to avoid unintended ties/duplicates.

views.name: icoads_ship_observation_sequences_win
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS table_suffix,
  callsign,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  hour,
  TIMESTAMP(
    FORMAT(
      '%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d',
      COALESCE(year,0),
      COALESCE(month,0),
      COALESCE(day,0),
      CAST(FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0)) AS INT64),
      CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 60) AS INT64),
      CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 3600) AS INT64)
    )
  ) AS obs_timestamp_approx,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) AS wind_speed_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) AS sea_surface_temp_c,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) AS sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  LAG(
    TIMESTAMP(
      FORMAT(
        '%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d',
        COALESCE(year,0),
        COALESCE(month,0),
        COALESCE(day,0),
        CAST(FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0)) AS INT64),
        CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 60) AS INT64),
        CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 3600) AS INT64)
      )
    )
  ) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS prev_obs_timestamp_approx,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(
    TIMESTAMP(
      FORMAT(
        '%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d',
        COALESCE(year,0),
        COALESCE(month,0),
        COALESCE(day,0),
        CAST(FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0)) AS INT64),
        CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 60) AS INT64),
        CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 3600) AS INT64)
      )
    ),
    LAG(
      TIMESTAMP(
        FORMAT(
          '%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d',
          COALESCE(year,0),
          COALESCE(month,0),
          COALESCE(day,0),
          CAST(FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0)) AS INT64),
          CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 60) AS INT64),
          CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 3600) AS INT64)
        )
      )
    ) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour),
    SECOND
  ) AS seconds_since_prev_approx,
  latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_lat_deg,
  longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_lon_deg,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed,10.0) - LAG(SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed,10.0)) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_wind_speed_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp,10.0) - LAG(SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp,10.0)) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) AS delta_sst_c
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000`
grain: one row per observation for each callsign with windowed differences to previous observation of same callsign

params.description: Provides one row per ICOADS observation per callsign with an approximate timestamp and windowed differences to the previous observation for the same callsign (time difference and deltas for latitude, longitude, wind speed, sea surface temperature, and sea level pressure).
params.when_to_use: Compute vessel/observer movement or environmental change between consecutive ICOADS observations for the same callsign (e.g., speed/heading estimation from delta lat/lon, change in wind or SST over time). | As a base for time-series analyses per callsign where you need the previous-observation context (seconds since previous observation, previous observation timestamp). | Filtering or anomaly detection that requires both current and immediately-previous observation values (e.g., sudden jump in position or measurement). | Composing further aggregations (e.g., average seconds-between-observations per callsign, distribution of deltas) by grouping this view's rows.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: placeholder column; set to NULL in this view (NULL literal in SELECT). | callsign: callsign of the observation (sourced from base column callsign). | year: observation year integer (sourced from base column year). | month: observation month integer (sourced from base column month). | day: observation day integer (sourced from base column day). | hour: observation hour as fractional hours (sourced from base column hour). | obs_timestamp_approx: approximate TIMESTAMP constructed from year, month, day, hour (derived from FORMAT(...) and TIMESTAMP(...)). | latitude: observation latitude (sourced from base column latitude). | longitude: observation longitude (sourced from base column longitude). | wind_speed_m_s: wind_speed divided by 10.0 to convert stored integer to m/s (derived from SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0)). | sea_surface_temp_c: sea_surface_temp divided by 10.0 to convert stored integer to degrees C (derived from SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0)). | sea_level_pressure_hpa: sea_level_pressure divided by 10.0 to convert stored integer to hPa (derived from SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0)). | prev_obs_timestamp_approx: the previous obs_timestamp_approx for the same callsign using LAG() OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) (derived TIMESTAMP similar to obs_timestamp_approx). | seconds_since_prev_approx: TIMESTAMP_DIFF between obs_timestamp_approx and prev_obs_timestamp_approx in seconds (derived using TIMESTAMP_DIFF). | delta_lat_deg: difference in latitude between current and previous observation for same callsign (latitude - previous latitude; implemented implicitly by comparing current latitude to the row returned by the partitioned lag — in this view the explicit expression is present as delta_lat_deg). | delta_lon_deg: difference in longitude between current and previous observation for same callsign (longitude - previous longitude). | delta_wind_speed_m_s: difference in wind_speed_m_s between current and previous observation for same callsign (wind_speed_m_s - previous wind_speed_m_s). | delta_sst_c: difference in sea_surface_temp_c between current and previous observation for same callsign (sea_surface_temp_c - previous sea_surface_temp_c).
params.grounded_columns: callsign | year | month | day | hour | latitude | longitude | wind_speed | sea_surface_temp | sea_level_pressure
params.metric: obs_timestamp_approx = TIMESTAMP(FORMAT('%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d', COALESCE(year,0), COALESCE(month,0), COALESCE(day,0), CAST(FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0)) AS INT64), CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 60) AS INT64), CAST(FLOOR((COALESCE(hour,0) - FLOOR(COALESCE(hour,0))) * 3600) AS INT64))) | wind_speed_m_s = SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) | sea_surface_temp_c = SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) | sea_level_pressure_hpa = SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) | prev_obs_timestamp_approx = LAG(obs_timestamp_approx) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour)  -- implemented in SQL by repeating the TIMESTAMP(...) expression inside LAG() | seconds_since_prev_approx = TIMESTAMP_DIFF(obs_timestamp_approx, prev_obs_timestamp_approx, SECOND) | delta_lat_deg = latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) | delta_lon_deg = longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) | delta_wind_speed_m_s = wind_speed_m_s - LAG(wind_speed_m_s) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour) | delta_sst_c = sea_surface_temp_c - LAG(sea_surface_temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY callsign ORDER BY year, month, day, hour)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-callsign (or one-row-per-callsign-per-time if keys include time) on corresponding key(s) — safe because this view is one-row-per-observation-per-callsign so joining a one-row-per-callsign dimension will not multiply rows. Example: JOIN to a callsign-to-vessel_dim on callsign (safe because vessel_dim must be one row per callsign). | Do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many relative to this view's row identity (one observation row) without first aggregating or deduplicating the other side. For example, do NOT join to a raw observations table or any events table that can contain multiple rows per callsign+timestamp unless you aggregate those rows first; doing so will multiply this view's rows and duplicate the windowed deltas/seconds measures. | If you need to enrich with many-to-one relationships keyed by (callsign, obs_timestamp_approx) where the enrichment side can contain multiple rows (e.g., sensor_readings with multiple channels at same timestamp), first aggregate sensor_readings to one row per callsign+timestamp (e.g., MAX or SUM) and then join — this preserves the intended cardinality and prevents measure duplication. | When composing upward aggregations from this view (e.g., average seconds_between_obs per callsign), aggregate this view's numeric measures after join or before joining wider one-to-many tables so you avoid accidental multiplication of intervals/deltas. | This view's window functions partition by callsign and order by year, month, day, hour; any join that changes or expands the set of rows per callsign (for example adding multiple matching rows for the same observation timestamp) will change the logical 'previous' relation if done before recomputing windows — to preserve correct prev_obs relations, compute windows in this view and then join externally (i.e., treat this view as canonical for prev/delta calculations).

views.name: earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  event_ts AS event_timestamp_utc,
  magnitude_type,
  magnitude_value
FROM (
  SELECT
    id,
    year,
    month,
    day,
    SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(month,1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(day,1) AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS event_ts,
    eq_mag_mw,
    eq_mag_ms,
    eq_mag_mb,
    eq_mag_ml,
    eq_mag_mfa,
    eq_mag_unk,
    eq_primary
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
)
UNPIVOT (
  magnitude_value FOR magnitude_type IN (eq_mag_mw AS 'MW', eq_mag_ms AS 'MS', eq_mag_mb AS 'MB', eq_mag_ml AS 'ML', eq_mag_mfa AS 'MFA', eq_mag_unk AS 'UNK', eq_primary AS 'PRIMARY')
)
WHERE magnitude_value IS NOT NULL
grain: id, magnitude_type -- one row per event per available magnitude type

params.description: A reshaped/unpivoted view that returns one row per earthquake event id and magnitude type, with the event date/timestamp and the reported magnitude value and its type.
params.when_to_use: List or filter earthquake magnitudes by event and magnitude type (e.g., show all MW magnitudes or compare MW vs ML for events). | Aggregate magnitudes across events by type (e.g., average MW per year) — use this view as the measure source and then GROUP BY magnitude_type. | Join earthquake magnitudes to event-level metadata (location, impact) when you need one row per event-magnitude combination. | Build time-series or seasonal analyses of magnitudes (year/month/day) where magnitude values are the metric of interest. | Normalize downstream queries so they don't need UNPIVOT logic — useful when composing across different magnitude columns uniformly.
params.output_schema: id: earthquake event identifier from base table (`bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.id`) | year: event year from base table (`...earthquakes.year`) | month: event month from base table (`...earthquakes.month`) — may be NULL in source and COALESCE'd to 1 when building event_timestamp_utc, but the output month column is the original month value | day: event day from base table (`...earthquakes.day`) — may be NULL in source and COALESCE'd to 1 when building event_timestamp_utc, but the output day column is the original day value | event_timestamp_utc: derived TIMESTAMP parsed from year, month, day using SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year,'-',LPAD(COALESCE(month,1),2,'0'),'-',LPAD(COALESCE(day,1),2,'0'))) — represents a best-effort UTC date for the event constructed from year/month/day | magnitude_type: the magnitude column name mapped to a short code (one of 'MW','MS','MB','ML','MFA','UNK','PRIMARY') produced by the UNPIVOT expression (derived from the column aliases in the UNPIVOT clause) | magnitude_value: numeric magnitude value taken from the corresponding magnitude column (eq_mag_mw, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk, eq_primary) — only non-NULL magnitudes are included
params.metric: magnitude_value = direct value from one of the source magnitude columns (eq_mag_mw | eq_mag_ms | eq_mag_mb | eq_mag_ml | eq_mag_mfa | eq_mag_unk | eq_primary) — this is not an aggregate, it's a reshaped scalar measure per (id, magnitude_type) | event_timestamp_utc = SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(month,1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(day,1) AS STRING),2,'0')))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level dimension tables (for example, any events_core / earthquakes_core_events_sel-like view keyed by id) on id — safe because this view is one row per (id, magnitude_type) so joining by id does NOT duplicate magnitude_value per (id, magnitude_type) if the target is strictly one row per id (one-to-one or many-to-one from this view to the dimension). | You may aggregate this view to event-level (GROUP BY id) before joining to one-to-many tables to avoid duplication. Example safe pattern: first compute event-level metrics like MAX(magnitude_value) FILTER(WHERE magnitude_type='MW') by grouping on id, then join to a one-to-many table. | Do NOT join this view directly to other tables/views that are one-to-many relative to (id, magnitude_type) (for example, event reports or many observation rows per event) without re-aggregating either side — such joins will multiply rows and therefore multiply magnitude_value occurrences, producing incorrect totals/averages. | When composing with sibling RESHAPE/UNPIVOT views (e.g., tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot or icoads_measures_unpivot_reshape), join on (id, magnitude_type) only if both are at the same grain and represent the same kind of measure; otherwise prefer joining on id and keeping magnitude_type separate or aggregating by id first. | When aggregating across magnitude_type, use explicit grouping by magnitude_type to preserve correct measure semantics (e.g., AVG(magnitude_value) GROUP BY magnitude_type). | If you need event_timestamp_utc as a strict point-in-time key for joins, be aware it is constructed from year/month/day (month/day may be NULL in source and are coerced to 1 when parsing); verify this behavior if exact original timestamps are required.

views.description: Unpivot the multiple magnitude columns into a canonical (magnitude_type, magnitude_value) pair per event. Use this when you need to compare magnitudes across scales or rank events by any magnitude type. | Use for: Rank or filter events by magnitude across different magnitude scales; Compare primary magnitude vs alternative magnitude scales; Aggregate event counts above magnitude thresholds irrespective of scale by choosing a magnitude_type

views.name: earthquakes_rank_by_magnitude_win
views.body_sql:

  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  latitude,

  COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) AS chosen_magnitude,
